title: Symbo Manual
text: Symbo identifies whether two molecules can feasibly assemble higher-order geometric structures (e.g., tetrahedra, face/edge capped cubes, etc.). Symbo requires: Two molecules annotated proper rotation axes User-supplied information bind one another Symbo tests compatible shape classes determines ones can form valid supramolecular structures. Symbo exclusively assesses geometric feasibility different structures (based symmetry properties user-defined binding constraints). consider physical properties molecular structures.

what: Step 2: Loading and Inspecting Your Molecules
title: Symbo Manual
text: Now ’ve prepared mol2 molecules, load R ensure everything worked ok. loading packages run following code prevent 3D plots trying render local graphics engine instead render exclusively web based viewer. parsing mol2 files using read_mol() function structures package (automatically installed alongside symbo). run mol2 files replace calls system.file() string path file interest (e.g. "/Users/username/Documents/my_molecule_1.mol2") Lets investigate molecules printing summary see molecule 1 (iron tripod) contains 83 atoms, 3 dummy atoms representing palladium binding position. Task Print summary molecule2 way.
code: options(rgl.useNULL=TRUE) # Load the libraries we need library(structures) # For reading mol2 files and annotating molecular structures library(chemviewR) # For visualising 3D molecular structures library(symbo) # For assessing geometrical feasibility of higher level structures  # Parse Molecules molecule1_filepath <- system.file(package = "symbo", "fe_dummies.mol2") molecule1 <- read_mol2(molecule1_filepath)  molecule2_filepath <- system.file(package = "symbo", "pd_dummies.mol2") molecule2 <- read_mol2(molecule2_filepath) #> Warning in format_atoms(atoms): Unexpected atom types found: [Pd]. Replacing #> these with 'Any' print(molecule1) #> =================== #> Chemical Molecule3D #> =================== #> Name: fe_dummies #> Atoms: 83 (3 dummy atoms) #> Bonds: 93 #> Molecule type: SMALL #> Charge type: NO_CHARGES #> ------------------- #> Symmetry Elements: 0 #> Symmetry Axes: 0 #> Symmetry Orders (Cn):  #> ------------------- #> See @atoms paramater for atom positions #> See @bonds paramater for bond positions #> See @symmetry_elements for symmetry elements

title: Symbo Manual
text: Symbo requires molecule annotated least one proper rotation axes (Cn) describe symmetry.

title: Symbo Manual
code: # Iron tripods have a C3 proper rotation axis.  # This axis is identical to the normal of the plane formed by our three N5 nitrogen atoms. So lets first compute this plane molecule1_plane <- molecule1 |>   filter_atoms_by_name("N5") |>   compute_plane_from_atoms()  ## Then we can create a 'ProperRotationAxis' object based on the plane_normal & centroid of the 3 N5 irons c3_axis_iron_tripod <- ProperRotationAxis(       n = 3, # Axis order; as in (Cn)       posA = molecule1_plane$centroid,       direction = molecule1_plane$normal   )  ## Annotate our molecule with this ProperRotationAxis molecule1 <- molecule1 |>   add_symmetry_element_to_molecule(c3_axis_iron_tripod)  # Visualise The plot to see if it worked plot_molecule(molecule1)

title: Symbo Manual
code: # Palladium has a C4 symmetry axis. # Direction is equivalent to the normal or the plane formed by the entire molecule # (including all four dummy atoms) so lets compute that plane molecule2_plane <- molecule2 |>   compute_plane_from_atoms()  ## Then we create a 'ProperRotationAxis' object based on the plane_normal & centroid of the entire molecule c4_axis_palladium <- ProperRotationAxis(   n = 4, # Axis order; as in (Cn)   posA = molecule2_plane$centroid,    direction = molecule2_plane$normal )   # Then we annotate our molecule with this information molecule2 <- molecule2 |>   add_symmetry_element_to_molecule(c4_axis_palladium)  # Plot the molecule to make the axis is present plot_molecule(molecule2)

title: Symbo Manual
text: find optimal configuration two molecules higher-order geometric structure might form, run: evaluated shape class returns two diagnostic values: Minimised Sum Squared Distances (D) D=d12+d22 D = d_1^2 + d_2^2 : d1d_1 = distance mol1 dummy → mol2 binding atom d2d_2 = distance mol2 dummy → mol1 binding atom lower value means geometrically feasible arrangement. Angle Dummy Binding Vectors () angle (radians) : vector mol1 dummy → mol1 binding atom vector mol2 dummy → mol2 binding atom perfectly aligned arrangement approaches π radians (~180°). shape class evaluated, Symbo reports two values:
code: # Specify the binding atom optimisations <- screen_molecules(   molecule1 = molecule1,   molecule2 = molecule2,    mol1_binding_atom = 7, # One of the N5 Nitrogens   mol2_binding_atom = 1  # Palladium atom ) #> ℹ Figuring out which shape classes are assessable #> ℹ Molecule 1 [fe_dummies] has [C3] #> ℹ Molecule 2 [pd_dummies] has [C4] #> ℹ Molecules [fe_dummies] and [pd_dummies] can be assessed for [1] shape class (Face-capped cube). #>  #> ── Face-capped cube ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ℹ Searching for optimal arrangement of molecules #> ℹ Fetching the first dummy atom bonded to each binding atom #> ℹ Rotating molecules so Symmetry Axes align with target vectors #> ℹ Extracting Symmetry Axes #> ℹ Fetching the first dummy atom bonded to each binding atom #> ℹ Rotating molecules so Symmetry Axes align with target vectors #> ℹ Extracting Symmetry Axes #> ℹ Running optimisation (this may take a moment) ... #>  #> ── Optimising + orientation ── #>  #> ── Optimising - orientation ── #>  #> ── Comparing all optimisation runs ── #>   # View result summary print(optimisations) #> ================================ #> Optimisation Result Collection #> ================================ #> Shape Classes Evaluated: 1 #> -> Face-capped cube (D: 0.000000 | A: 3.141587 | O: -)
